title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Asha Raman
content:
Overview

This playbook describes Redwood Inference's standardized approach for producing and maintaining developer-facing documentation in the Developer Experience (DevEx) area: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is consistent, high-quality docs that reduce onboarding time, lower support load, and make SDKs and examples trustworthy for production use.

Intended audience
- Developer Experience (DevEx) engineers and tech writers
- SDK owners and maintainers
- Developer-facing on-call and support engineers
- Product and platform engineers who publish public examples

Principles
1. Small, tested examples: every code example must be runnable and minimal.
2. Single source of truth: canonical API examples live in the SDK repo and are referenced by the docs site.
3. Templates for reproducibility: quickstarts and templates are parameterized (environment variables) and include scripts for local setup.
4. Observable docs quality: track example test pass-rate and support-incidence correlation.
5. Fast review loop: changes to examples require automated checks + at least one reviewer from DevEx or owning SDK team.

Document types and where they live
- SDK guides: deep-dive usage and migration guides; location: confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates + linked to SDK repos.
- Quickstarts & templates: minimal projects (CLI, web, serverless) that get a developer from zero to a working Redwood request in <10 minutes.
- API examples: snippets for endpoint usage (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, streaming, function calls). Canonical examples stored in SDK mono-repo under /examples/canonical and mirrored here.
- Docs site operating procedures: publishing steps, release cadence, rollback, and metrics checks.
- Top support issues & canonical fixes: triaged, reproducible issues with step-by-step debug and fix guidance for support engineers and customers.

Roles and ownership
- Owner: Developer Experience (engineering) - primary for templates, site ops, and canonical fixes.
- SDK maintainers: engineering team owning each SDK (python-sdk, js-sdk, go-sdk). Responsible for canonical examples, tests, and CI.
- DevEx writer: responsible for high-level guides and quickstart copy.
- On-call/support: responsible for validating canonical fixes and adding new entries when a repeated issue is observed.

Standards for content quality
- Metadata: every doc must include title, summary, prerequisites, tested-on SDK version, and last-updated.
- Example tests: all code snippets must be covered by a unit/integration test in the SDK examples CI. Failure to include tests blocks publishing.
- Tagging: include labels for platform (python/js/go), feature (chat/embeddings/streaming), and stability (experimental/stable/deprecated).
- Accessibility & language: short paragraphs, active voice, and clear step numbers for procedures.

Quickstarts and template checklist
- README with purpose and TL;DR run instructions.
- Environment variables documented in .env.example with clear notes about secrets (use Redwood test key or local stub).
- One-command local run (./dev.sh or npm run dev).
- CI job that spins up example, runs smoke test (hit health endpoint, run a sample inference).
- License and attribution if third-party code is used.

Canonical API examples (required patterns)
- Simple generation (sync): show endpoint call for text generation with prompt, temperature, max_tokens. Include sample output.
- Streaming generation: show chunked response handling and reconnection strategy.
- Chat example: system+user+assistant turn management and multi-turn KV cache guidance.
- Embeddings: single and batched examples and recommended batching size for throughput.
- Function/tool calling: payload format and security considerations (sanitizing tool results).
- Error handling: pattern for transient errors (exponential backoff), quota errors (429 handling), and model-fallback.

Example: Python sync generation snippet (canonical)
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-small", prompt="Summarize the following:

- What is Redwood?", max_tokens=150, temperature=0.2)
print(resp.text)
```
Notes: the canonical snippet above must exist in python-sdk/examples/canonical/generation_test.py and have a CI job that validates the call using a recorded HTTP fixture.

Docs site operating procedures (publish flow)
1. Draft locally in confluence or Markdown in the docs repo.
2. Ensure canonical examples are up-to-date and tests are green.
3. Open a PR against the docs site with the following checklist: PR body includes short summary, affected SDKs, and test results.
4. Automated checks: markdown lint, example test pass, link-check, broken-image-check, and accessibility check.
5. Reviewer: at least one SDK owner + one DevEx reviewer must approve.
6. Merge and CI deploy: deploy to staging website and run smoke visual + example tests.
7. Monitoring: check docs site error budget (broken links, 5xx) and track support incidence for the doc URL for 14 days.
8. Rollback: if staging fails or support incidence increases by >50% relative to baseline, revert the change and open an incident review.

Release cadence and versioning
- Minor content updates: weekly sprint (fast-tracked if they fix support-blocking issues).
- Major rewrites or SDK migrations: coordinate with SDK owners; schedule a docs freeze 48 hours prior to SDK release.
- Versioning: when SDK introduces breaking changes, docs must include migration guide with code diffs and example conversions.

Top support issues (triage + canonical fixes)
- Issue: SDK auth errors after rotate of API key
  - Symptom: 401 on every request immediately after key rotation.
  - Root cause: customer app config still uses the old key; some long-running workers cached old credentials.
  - Canonical fix: rotate keys with a staged rollout: 1) create new key, 2) update ephemeral workers and rotate, 3) update long-running workers and restart, 4) deprecate old key after 48h. Add sample restart script and health-check step.
- Issue: Embeddings throughput regressions
  - Symptom: sudden drop in embeddings/s after SDK update.
  - Root cause: SDK changed default batching policy; customer uses small batch sizes leading to higher per-item overhead.
  - Canonical fix: revert to previous batching config or increase batch_size to recommended value (see example config). Add sample config snippet and a benchmark command.
- Issue: Streaming reconnect behavior loses partial output
  - Symptom: client reconnects and receives only final chunk or duplicates.
  - Root cause: client-level buffering and lack of idempotent chunk sequence handling.
  - Canonical fix: implement client chunk sequence numbers and resume policy using last-acknowledged token. Provide canonical JS and Python reconnection snippets.
- Issue: High latency for short requests in production
  - Symptom: 95th p99 latency elevated for short prompt sizes.
  - Root cause: batching policy aggressive to optimize throughput, causing queueing tail latency.
  - Canonical fix: add per-route latency SLO override to bypass batching (route config example below) or enable low-latency instance pool.

Route config example for low-latency override (YAML snippet)
```yaml
routes:
  - name: chat-low-latency
    model: redwood-1-latency
    latency_override_ms: 50
    batching_policy: disabled
```

Operational metrics and dashboards to track
- Example test pass rate (per SDK) - target: 100%
- Docs link-check failures - target: 0 per week
- Support incidents referencing docs URLs - target: downward trend month-over-month
- Time-to-first-successful-request for quickstarts - target: <10 minutes for 90% of users

Onboarding checklist for a new SDK owner
1. Read this playbook and review existing canonical examples for your SDK.
2. Ensure SDK repo contains /examples/canonical with tests and a smoke CI job.
3. Add yourself to the SDK owners section in the docs metadata.
. 4. Schedule a 30-min sync with DevEx to review publishing process and label taxonomy.

Appendix: canonical fixes table (summary)
- Key rotation: staged rollout + restart steps
- Embeddings regressions: batching config + benchmark commands
- Streaming reconnects: sequence numbers + resume policy
- Short-request latency: per-route override + low-latency pool
- 429/quota errors: client backoff policy + quota dashboard link

Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: devex-oncall@redwood.example.com (DevEx on-call)
- Slack channels: #devex, #sdk-python, #sdk-js
- For security-sensitive examples or customer-reported data leaks, contact security@redwood.example.com immediately and set confidentiality: restricted on the Confluence page.
